append.text: Ps 52:2 *abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus* (no *suis*, where 13:1b has *in stúdiis suis* and 105:43 *in iniquitátibus suis*) → *abomináveis nas iniquidades* — no possessive supplied; *nas suas iniquidades* (MS1932) option. 50:7 *in iniquitátibus concéptus sum* is the same phrase.

Ps 52:6b *confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos* → *foram envergonhados, porque Deus os desprezou* (D15). The stylist asked *ficaram envergonhados* («stiff, bookish passive») — refused, option: *ficar envergonhado* is a feeling, *confúsi sunt* is being put to shame; the Latinist passed it twice.

**Ps 52:6b *dissipávit ossa* → *dispersou os ossos*** — bones take *dispersar*, as 21:15 *foram dispersos todos os meus ossos* (dispérgere, the same Greek family διασκορπίζω). Proposal for the row: *dispersar* for people and for things strewn (bones); *dissipar* for what is undone (the law 118:126, designs 32:10). *dissipou* (MS1932) option; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked.
Ps 52:1 copies 13:1a; the blind reader of Ps 52 listed *insensato* as unknown (the first time) — kept.

append.row: | esca / cibus (*sicut escam panis*, *ut cibum panis*) |
append.text: **Ps 52:5 *ut cibum panis* → *como quem come pão*, copied from 13:4.** The Latinist of Ps 52 asked *como alimento de pão* on both reads (minor), the stylist offered *como se come o pão* (the *como … come* jingle, which he said to keep) — both refused for the twin, options in Ps 52's decision `cibum`. The same Latinist remark has now been refused three times across the twins.

**Ps 52:7 *cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ* → *quando Deus fizer voltar o cativeiro do seu povo*** — the convértere row's verb, causative, as the stylist asked. Draft 1 had *reverter o cativeiro* (the same root; 'undo'), refused by the stylist as juridical and listed unknown by the blind reader; the feared hearing 'bring the captivity back again' was raised by no reader (not yet tested blind in this form). 125:1 *In converténdo … captivitátem Sion*, 125:4 *Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram* (→ *Fazei voltar, Senhor, o nosso cativeiro*) should follow. *fizer voltar os cativos*, *reverter* options.
Ps 52:7 *convérterit … captivitátem* → *fizer voltar o cativeiro* (causative, as 9:4 *Ao fazer voltar para trás*); see the row *captívitas*.

**Ps 52 done (draft 2):** every shared wording copied from Ps 13 draft 3 (checked against D1–D43: none ruled against since); decided locally only where the Latin differs — 52:2 *nas iniquidades*, 52:6 *A Deus não invocaram* (13:5's order kept for the twin), 52:6b whole, 52:7 *quando Deus fizer voltar o cativeiro*. Reader remarks on shared words (52:2 *fizeram-se*, 52:5 *alimento de pão* / *como se come o pão*, 52:7 the -ará pair) were refused to keep the twins identical: if Gustavo takes one, it goes into both psalms.

terms: | placére + dative (*qui homínibus placent*) | agradar a (*dos que agradam aos homens*) | open | Ps 52:6b (ἀνθρωπαρέσκων, 'men-pleasers'); 114:9 *Placébo Dómino* should take *agradarei ao Senhor*. The Latin's openness (pleasing to men / courting them) kept; MS1932's *procuram agradar* closes it (option). The blind reader heard people-pleasers first. |
